finding.claim: The unauthenticated POST /hooks/test endpoint sends a server-side HTTP POST to a URL taken from the request body. There is no scheme, host or IP validation, so an anonymous caller can make the server reach internal services or cloud metadata endpoints. The response status is returned, which gives a blind probe oracle.

trace.note: pub router created with no auth middleware
upstream status code returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, scheme check, hostname or IP-range blocklist, DNS resolution check, or redirect restriction. requireAdmin is applied only to the admin router (routes.js:12), not to pub. I could not see how the routers are mounted, because only routes.js exists in the directory.

verdict.reason: routes.js:20 passes req.body.callback straight to axios.post with no validation, the pub router (routes.js:4) has no auth (requireAdmin is only applied to admin at routes.js:12), and routes.js:21 returns the upstream status; the mount point is not visible, but nothing in routes.js restricts pub.

finding.claim: The admin GET /diagnostics/fetch endpoint fetches an arbitrary URL from a query parameter with no destination validation. It is reachable only by admin sessions, so the impact is lower. It is still SSRF to internal networks and metadata endpoints, and an attacker with an admin session or an XSS/CSRF foothold could abuse it.
finding.guards_checked: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10) checks req.session.role === 'admin', which is a real authorization guard but does not limit the destination. There is no URL allowlist, scheme check, private-IP blocking, or redirect limit. Whether this router is mounted at all is unverified.

verdict.guard_found: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10, applied at :12) restricts access to admin sessions; there is no destination validation (allowlist, scheme, private-IP or redirect check).
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (routes.js:12-16 passes req.query.url straight to axios.get), but the source is not reachable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker because requireAdmin at routes.js:8/12 returns 403 unless session.role is "admin", and no file mounts the admin router, so the finding fails the attacker-controlled source check.
